message.content: {"summary":"You present a clearly organised report with a defensible no-ship conclusion, identify important stakeholders, and use external examples and a professional code. To strengthen it, assess the specific defect and its risks, support business claims with evidence, and explain whether repair, delay, and retesting could enable safe delivery. More precise references, clearer writing, and suitable visual evidence would also improve the report.","next_steps":["In “DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship,” assess the defect’s severity and likelihood, identify possible harm and risk controls, and set test-based criteria for whether repaired servers could be shipped safely. Support claims about competitive advantage and future quality improvement with evidence.","In “RECOMMENDATION,” compare refusing the contract with notifying the client, delaying delivery, correcting the defects, and retesting. Explain how your proposed decision protects each stakeholder and meets the client’s needs; in “The Most Ethical Path,” clarify the limits of the NHS comparison.","Revise the “References” for completeness and consistent formatting, correct language errors, and consider adding a table or diagram that summarises the risks, controls, and stakeholder impacts. Use relevant qualitative and quantitative evidence to strengthen your case. "],"criteria":{"C1":"Your “INTRODUCTION” links quality and safety to business competition and identifies stakeholders. For the next level, Excellent, develop several distinct ethical issues in greater depth and show how both organisational pressures and each stakeholder’s interests shape the dilemma.","C2":"“DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship” presents arguments on both sides, and “RECOMMENDATION” gives a clear conclusion. For the next level, Very good, examine the trade-offs objectively and in greater depth, avoid unsupported claims, and draw out what different stakeholders should do.","C3":"Your pro/con structure and use of the NHS example, professional code, and reputation argument lead logically to a no-ship conclusion. For the next level, Very good, make the case more compelling by assessing the actual defect risk and showing how repair, mitigation, and retesting affect your conclusion.","C4":"You use relevant external examples and a professional code, but some claims lack support and one reference is incomplete. For the next level, Very good, substantiate the key arguments with complete references and a balanced range of qualitative and quantitative evidence, including evidence specific to the defect and its risks.","C5":"Your report includes an abstract, introduction, body, conclusion, and recommendation, and is generally readable. For the next level, Good, improve fluency by correcting language errors, use a few relevant visual elements to support the discussion, and make the references complete and consistent."}}
